newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Busang to flare investor discontent in miners.
newsitem.headline: Busang to flare investor discontent in miners.

text.p: A shock statement that Indonesia's Busang deposit, once thought to contain 71 million ounces of gold, was not economic would scare investors away from small Canadian and Australian gold explorers, analysts said on Monday.

"It's particularly devastating for the Canadian sector in particular, but it will wash over the rest of the sector because we have got a gold price at four-years lows and the Australian dollar gold price at virtually 10-year lows," ANZ Securities gold analyst David Kauler said.

"It is going to make the regulatory regime take a tougher stance on reporting standards and you'll probably see the Canadian sector swing towards Australian-style reporting standards on resources and reserves," Kauler said.
The Busang announcement by Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd had an immediate impact on the shares of small explorer Golden Valley Mines NL which fell to a 12-month low.

Perth-based Golden Valley, which had a claim over a portion of the Busang deposit in partnership with an Indonesian company PT Krueng Gasui, was trading 12 cents lower at 40 cents at 2.05 p.m. (0405 GMT).
The stock has swung wildly in recent months as the controversy about the Busang deposit affected investor sentiment in the Australian and Canadian markets.
Golden Valley president Warren Beckwith was overseas on Monday and not immediately available for comment, his office said.

Other local gold stocks weakened after the Bre-X statement hit the local market towards the end of morning trade, including Delta Gold NL and Sons of Gwalia. Delta Gold was nine cents lower at A$2.01 just before the start of the afternoon session while Sons of Gwalia was eight cents lower at A$5.50. The Australian Gold Index, six points lower before the Bre-X statement, fell another three points.

Bre-X said in its shock statement that the most recent batch of assay results from Busang in the province of East Kalimantan had not produced any gold of economic interest. This was in contrast to the 71 million ounces of gold which Bre-X had earlier said was confidently believed to be present at Busang, making it the world's richest lode discovery this century.
The Australian Mining Industry Council said it had no official comment on the latest Bre-X statement or the wider Busang controvery.
"Of course we have watched the Busang statements with interest," a council spokesman said.
Brokers said the Australian gold sector would probably face some downward share pressure.
"The effect is likely to be negative as it will make investors more sceptical about the information given in future gold finds," one Sydney-based broker said.
"The malaise in the gold sector, with the weaker gold price, is set to continue for some time with the Bre-X situtation," said Mark Pervan at brokerage firm Daiwa Securities.
ANZ's Kauler said the impact of the Busang controversy would affect both the gold price and the more speculative stocks listed in Australia as well.
"In the short term there's going to be a certain amount of fallout here because the stocks that have promoted themselves as 'blue sky' will have a bit of a shakeout," he said.
"There's some obvious candidates here that promote 'blue sky' more than others, and particularly those stocks with a strong offshore holding and strong North American holdings."

"You won't have this 70 million ounce deposit there and three million ounces a year that's not coming onto the market. If you're not going to have these dramatic projects coming through because they don't exist, then it doesn't put so much pressure on the supply/demand curve," he said.
